This file documents the trade_summaries resource at the shell, one section per command. Every command is a subcommand of =trade_summaries=, and every section exports its own script into =projects/ores.shell/scripts/library/=. Loading a script runs that one command, so a failure names the command it came from.

* Commands

** =list=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: E8F1E241-D825-5F5D-83D1-E983DE38AFB1
:END:

Reads one page of the collection. Nothing addresses it but the caller's tenant, so it is the read that shows what exists.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
trade_summaries list [--offset <n>] [--limit <n>] [--order <field>] [--desc]
#+end_example

It is addressed at =trading.v1.trade_summaries.list=.

#+name: trade_summaries-list
#+begin_src ores-shell :tangle trade_summaries-list.ores :exports none
trade_summaries list --limit 1
#+end_src

** =get=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: 2CFF987F-9D49-5EB1-9E19-E6E0BAE20329
:END:

Reads the one row its key addresses. A key states every identifying column, so a partial key is refused rather than answered with an arbitrary row.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
trade_summaries get <id>
#+end_example

It is addressed at =trading.v1.trade_summaries.get=.

#+name: trade_summaries-get
#+begin_src ores-shell :tangle trade_summaries-get.ores :exports none
trade_summaries get 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
#+end_src

** =get-many=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: F22FA627-1CE2-507D-A7F9-A20CFFE0425B
:END:

Reads several rows in one request, one key group per row.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
